original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

actual_scope: Over F_2, at g=3 and d=2, with exactly one unsplit full call E_j on each stage, no two constant thin maps meet the paired-star endpoint at total rank 6 or 7. Every solution has rank sum at least 8, and 8 is attained.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed query demand removes real work. This session changes one hypothesis of the PR #5747 paired-star contract: each stage uses the single unsplit call E_j rather than two orthogonal halves. The field stays F_2 and the thin-map count stays at two. PR #6956 left this gap equation open after excluding three or more T-commuting projectors.
bottleneck_link: A two-map word of total rank 6 or 7 would have met the chronological floor of 6 at the smallest paired size under the one-unsplit-call schedule the determinant allows. Both affine families have minimum rank 8, so this schedule supplies neither a caller nor a change to the selected frontier 781451/250000000.
stop_rule: Stop after the entrywise gap census, the family A block-rank proof, and the exhaustive family B census. Do not search three thin maps, nonconstant entries, entries outside F_2, or g=13.
evidence: verify.py solves every order and gap pair, checks the polynomial word against the conjugation formula, enumerates both family A forms, and compiles search.c to visit all 2^32 family B parameters. It prints PASS_PAIRED_STAR_UNSPLIT_TWO_THIN. Python 3.12 and gcc.

open_questions.question: With one unsplit full call E_j on each stage, can three constant F_2 thin maps meet total rank 6 at g=3, d=2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Two constant maps now need total rank 8, so the chronological floor of 6 is still open under this call shape. The rank-6 word in PR #7011 uses two full calls per stage.
open_questions.first_step: Fix order (0, 1, 2), place three constant maps in three distinct gaps, and solve the three-term entry equation.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The equation is the two-gap equation of this package with one more gap.

open_questions.question: Can a thin map with entries in F_2[D_0, D_1, D_2] bring the unsplit two-map rank below 8?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The rank-8 minimum is proved only for constant entries. A stage-dependent entry would be a different contract.
open_questions.first_step: Let one diagonal block be linear in a single D_j and test the same family A and family B gap pairs.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. It drops the constant-entry hypothesis used here.
